choices: Recursive detrend: the time index is the calendar month count (year * 12 + month), so a gap in sii.csv is a gap in time rather than a shift of row index; for a contiguous series this is identical to the row index.

Recursive detrend: a residual is taken only where the fit has at least one degree of freedom, i.e. from the third observation of the series; the first two months carry no signal (their residual is identically zero or undefined) and are excluded.

Recursive detrend: the published index is used as supplied, on the clarification that an affine function of time leaves the recursive residual unchanged; missing SII values (blank, '.', 'NA') are dropped and a duplicated month is an error.
SII column: a header equal to 'SII' (case-insensitive, stripped) is preferred; otherwise the first header containing 'sii'.
NDX_t is the last non-missing FRED observation dated inside calendar month t, whatever day of the month that is; a partially covered final month is used as it stands.

RF_(t+1) is the compounded daily French RF over every daily row dated inside calendar month t+1; log(1 + RF) is formed as the sum of the daily log(1 + rf / 100); a month with no RF row is unavailable, a partially covered month is used as it stands.
Month t+1 is the next calendar month; a calendar month with no NDX observation breaks the pair on either side of it.

Aligned sample: every month t with x_t, NDX_t, NDX_(t+1) and RF_(t+1) available, in month order; first_signal_month and last_signal_month are the first and last such t (signal months, not return months).
Primary: OLS of y_(t+1) on x_t with intercept; rotations np.roll(x, k) for k = 12 .. n-12 inclusive (n_shifts = n - 23); a rotation counts if its slope <= b; p = (1 + count) / (1 + n_shifts).
Newey-West (nw_t and the Clark-West t): Bartlett weights 1 - j/(L+1), L = 3, no small-sample correction; applied to the OLS moment conditions for b and to the demeaned Clark-West loss for its mean.
Secondary: forecast for aligned pair i (0-based, i >= 120) is estimated on pairs 0..i-1; the benchmark is the mean of y over pairs 0..i-1; n_oos_forecasts = n - 120.
INSUFFICIENT (n < 240): per PREREG §2 no regression is run; every statistic is null and both criteria are null, which may not be read as a pass.
b_per_sd = b * sd(x, ddof=1); r2_in_sample is 1 - SSE/SST of the primary regression.
